entry.title: 3 US cities picked to host first women’s volleyball World Cup in North America
entry.summary: Three cities in the United States were selected as sites for the 2027 women's volleyball World Cup, the new name for the world championships, the sport's international governing body announced Thursday. The 32-nation tournament will be played in North America for the first time Aug. 20-Sept. 5. Pool play and round-of-16 matches will be played in Omaha, Nebraska, at the CHI Health Center Arena, and in Orlando, Florida, at the Kia Center. The Honda Center in Anaheim, California, will host the quarterfinals, semifinals and final and then serve as the host venue for the men's and women's indoor volleyball competition for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Host cities in Canada will be announced later. In March, FIVB announced the rebranding of the men's and women's world championships. The men's World Cup will be played in Poland. The tournament, previously played once every four years, will now be played every two years. The tournament is an Olympic qualifier, with the top three national teams not yet qualified for the 2028 Games earning spots. Sports and entertainment network ION will provide 17 days of coverage, including 19 live matches and 10 hours of studio show coverage. The network also will stream 45 matches. Italy defeated Turkey in five sets to win the 2025 championship in Bangkok, Thailand.

He opened the day by throwing passes across the international border — from one boat to another on the Niagara River — to former Bills receiver Stevie Johnson.And the Bills honored their cross-border fanbase by having both the U.S. and Canadian anthems performed with both countries’ flags displayed on the field.The Toronto musical group Barenaked Ladies was greeted by a loud cheer before singing “O, Canada.” They were followed by Hawaiian-born actress and singer Auli’i Cravalho performing “The Star-Spangled Banner.” U.S. pop group OneRepublic also performed at halftime, while set up on a platform in the stands at the north end of the field.RELATED STORY | Chicago Bears could merge 2 sites for potential stadium in northwest Indiana“It was crazy. M-V-P!”And the Bills even rolled out a new green grass carpet by choosing to resod the entire field ahead of schedule following their preseason finale against Pittsburgh on Aug. They did so after the original turf, which had been laid down in October, showed signs of wear and tear, and with large divots having to be replaced during two preseason games and two practices.Bills players indicated after practicing in the stadium on Tuesday that the grass felt firmer, and noticed a larger infill of sand. entry.summary: Martin County High School receives third bomb threat in eight days    WPBF
entry.article_text: Martin County High School received another threat through the state's FortifyFL reporting system, the third bomb threat involving our campus this week, the school district said Friday afternoon. "I recognize that you have heard from me repeatedly this week regarding safety-related disruptions on our campus," Principal Lori Vogel said in a message to families. The latest threat referenced two specific buildings, requiring students and staff to be evacuated while law enforcement conducted a thorough search. Students and staff were relocated to other areas of campus during the response. On Monday, students and staff were evacuated after a bomb threat prompted a response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Eight days ago, students and staff were evacuated in the afternoon after a bomb threat was received via email, according to school officials. In a message sent to families, school officials said all buildings were being evacuated at the direction of law enforcement while authorities investigate the threat. Vogel noted the seriousness of the threats. "Every threat must be taken seriously," the principal said. "Each report generates a significant law enforcement response, disrupts instruction, displaces students and staff, and creates understandable concern throughout our school community. Unlike many situations that may require an emergency response, the behavior prompting these repeated disruptions is entirely avoidable. We need our families as partners in addressing this behavior. Please speak directly with your children about the seriousness and far-reaching impact of making or participating in a false threat." The message added: "What a student may view as a joke or a temporary way to avoid class can have widespread consequences for an entire campus and community. FortifyFL is an important safety resource. Students and families who become aware of a credible threat—or who have a legitimate reason to believe questionable, dangerous or criminal activity may be occurring—should continue to report that information through FortifyFL. Information about submitting a report is available on our school's and the School District's websites. "However, FortifyFL must never be used to submit information that someone knows to be false," the message said. "The District has zero tolerance for anyone who knowingly misuses the platform or participates in making a false threat. Any individual found responsible will face severe school disciplinary consequences and potential criminal charges." The principal concluded: "We appreciate your partnership in reinforcing that false threats are neither harmless nor funny. They place an unacceptable burden on students, employees, families, law enforcement and the broader community—and they must stop.Thank you for your immediate attention to this serious matter and for partnering with us to maintain a safe, orderly learning environment for every student and staff member at Martin County High School. entry.title: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee - WPEC
entry.summary: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee    WPEC
entry.article_text: Health officials have issued a blue-green algae health alert for an area of Lake Okeechobee after water samples detected harmful toxins. The Florida Department of Health in Martin County said the alert covers the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area and was issued in response to samples collected Sept. The area is located on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County. Residents and visitors should use caution in and around the lake, officials said. People should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials also advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water, according to the department. Officials said contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins. Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure, health officials said. RELATED: 'Influence campaign': Okeechobee County leaders want to change Lake O's narrative Officials said it is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903 . Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure to a harmful algae bloom can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222 . Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090 .

entry.title: Vero Beach animal hospital manager accused of reclaiming cats, abandoning them outside - cw34.com
entry.summary: Vero Beach animal hospital manager accused of reclaiming cats, abandoning them outside    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A Vero Beach animal hospital manager was arrested after investigators said she reclaimed two cats from the Humane Society of Vero Beach and Indian River County, then abandoned them outdoors without care. Deanna Rae Wesley, 43, was arrested Sept. 15 on an active warrant charging her with two counts of animal abandonment, both first-degree misdemeanors, according to Indian River County court records. Animal Control investigators said Wesley, who works at Dr. Dan’s Animal Hospital , picked up two white-and-brown tabby cats from the Humane Society on Sept. Wesley reportedly told staff the cats were being returned to a caregiver, but she would not identify that person, the affidavit said. The next day, Animal Control received a complaint about a white-and-brown tabby cat crying at a resident’s front door. Investigators said the cat was taken to Animal Control, where its microchip and Humane Society staff confirmed it was one of the cats Wesley had picked up. An investigator said Wesley initially denied it was the same cat but acknowledged the matching microchip number. According to the affidavit, she declined to explain how the cat ended up loose at the home. The resident told investigators that a woman matching Wesley’s description, wearing a Dr. Dan’s T-shirt, spoke with her mother and warned her to watch out for Animal Control in the area. The woman allegedly called the cats colony cats, the affidavit said. See also: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs Animal Control recovered the second cat at the same residence Sept. Both cats were described as extremely friendly, with debris on their faces and chins. Investigators said the cats were not capable of surviving outdoors on their own and that no one was known to be caring for them. The warrant alleges Wesley abandoned the cats on a public street without providing care, food, protection or shelter. A judge set bond at $250 per count, for a total of $500.

entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WFLX
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday. Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. “Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” Flowers said. The operation’s targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff’s office said. During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. “Our team did a great job of getting him off the street,” Flowers said. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff’s office said. Victims’ advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. “We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this,” Flowers said. Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. “We’ve never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot,” he said. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. “This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it,” Williams said. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. “Our work is far from done,” Williams said. “This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today.” FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday. Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. “Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” Flowers said. The operation’s targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff’s office said. During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. “Our team did a great job of getting him off the street,” Flowers said. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff’s office said. Victims’ advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. “We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this,” Flowers said. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. “Our work is far from done,” Williams said. “This operation requires a lot of resources and time. entry.title: Midterm voting picks up amid massive shifts in voting districts
entry.summary: Election day is still 6 weeks away, but the first midterm ballots have already been cast. Early, in-person voting is now officially underway in Virginia, while voters in South Dakota, Idaho and Minnesota can file absentee ballots. You never know whats going to happen in the coming months, a Virginia voter told Scripps News Groups Richmond station WTVR . Early voting is a great way to get out there make sure that that your vote is counted. More voting is coming soon. 47 states and D.C. have no-excuse early voting periods with varying start dates. But as voters head to the polls, many could be confused about where theyre casting their ballots after an unprecedented wave of redistricting fights across the country. A recent report from the nonpartisan group Protect Democracy shows nearly 35 million voters have been assigned to different districts than during the 2024 election. Thats about 1 in 10 Americans. The new maps are driven by demands from President Trump to GOP state officials to ensure Republicans maintain control of Congress. This effort has been met by corresponding democratic moves. Some of the issues driving voter turnout, like affordability and immigration, are causing concerns within the GOP. Republican Florida Representative Maria Salazar challenged the president in a new campaign ad released Thursday. Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far, Rep. Salazar stated in her ad. The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today. MORE ON VOTING | Trump slams the Supreme Court for rejecting his push to restrict mail ballots Another major factor for candidates and their parties is funding. The projected advertising costs for the 2026 midterms is $11.6 billion , a total that would make it the most expensive election in U.S. history, surpassing even the 2024 presidential election, which amounted to a total of $11.2 billion spent on ads.

entry.title: Martin County High School receives third bomb threat in eight days - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County High School receives third bomb threat in eight days    WPBF
entry.article_text: Martin County High School received another threat through the state's FortifyFL reporting system, the third bomb threat involving our campus this week, the school district said Friday afternoon. "I recognize that you have heard from me repeatedly this week regarding safety-related disruptions on our campus," Principal Lori Vogel said in a message to families. The latest threat referenced two specific buildings, requiring students and staff to be evacuated while law enforcement conducted a thorough search. Students and staff were relocated to other areas of campus during the response. On Monday, students and staff were evacuated after a bomb threat prompted a response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Eight days ago, students and staff were evacuated in the afternoon after a bomb threat was received via email, according to school officials. In a message sent to families, school officials said all buildings were being evacuated at the direction of law enforcement while authorities investigate the threat. Vogel noted the seriousness of the threats. "Every threat must be taken seriously," the principal said. "Each report generates a significant law enforcement response, disrupts instruction, displaces students and staff, and creates understandable concern throughout our school community. Unlike many situations that may require an emergency response, the behavior prompting these repeated disruptions is entirely avoidable. We need our families as partners in addressing this behavior. Please speak directly with your children about the seriousness and far-reaching impact of making or participating in a false threat." The message added: "What a student may view as a joke or a temporary way to avoid class can have widespread consequences for an entire campus and community. FortifyFL is an important safety resource. Students and families who become aware of a credible threat—or who have a legitimate reason to believe questionable, dangerous or criminal activity may be occurring—should continue to report that information through FortifyFL. Information about submitting a report is available on our school's and the School District's websites. "However, FortifyFL must never be used to submit information that someone knows to be false," the message said. "The District has zero tolerance for anyone who knowingly misuses the platform or participates in making a false threat. Any individual found responsible will face severe school disciplinary consequences and potential criminal charges." The principal concluded: "We appreciate your partnership in reinforcing that false threats are neither harmless nor funny. They place an unacceptable burden on students, employees, families, law enforcement and the broader community—and they must stop.Thank you for your immediate attention to this serious matter and for partnering with us to maintain a safe, orderly learning environment for every student and staff member at Martin County High School. This is a breaking news story that will be updated

entry.article_text: Lucie road rage incident that escalated into a physical fight and shooting landed two men in handcuffs Thursday. Lucie Police Department, the incident happened at about 6:30 p.m. near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. Police said that before the shooting, one driver believed he was being followed after merging onto Southwest Crosstown Parkway. The vehicles had passed each other, and one driver believed the other had cut him off. Investigators determined there was no intentional following, police said. One of the drivers, identified as Tylon Kukielka, 57, was driving with his girlfriend to her home after leaving a local restaurant. The other driver, identified as Dean Plotts, 41, was traveling in the same direction. Police said the situation escalated into a physical fight near Southwest Brevity Terrace. During the fight, Kukielka allegedly fired his gun, striking Plotts twice in the left wrist and legs. See also: Formerly conjoined twins see each other face-to-face after historic separation surgery A St. Lucie County sheriff's deputy traveling in the area witnessed the incident and detained Kukielka. Plotts was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also taken to a hospital for a medical evaluation. Investigators recovered surveillance video and shell casings during the investigation. Detectives later charged Kukielka with attempted homicide. Plotts was charged with burglary with assault or battery. Both men were taken into custody. The incident remains under investigation.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie police arrest alleged drug dealer using dead man's phone - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie police arrest alleged drug dealer using dead man's phone    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Lucie Police say they used a dead man's own phone to text his alleged drug dealer and arrange a buy, an investigation that led to a search warrant, thousands in cash, guns and drugs found at the dealer's home. According to the arrest affidavit, officers responded to an apartment at 700 SE Collins Lane on September 13th for an overdose. They found 34-year-old Miqueias Oliveira Silva dead, with a bloody syringe and a bag of cocaine next to him. The affidavit says rigor mortis suggested Silva had been dead for about 24 hours. It’s destroying the community. It’s destroying the members of the community, said Magalys Koch, a substance abuse expert at Hibiscus Counseling. A neighbor who called 911 told police he last saw Silva getting out of the passenger side of a black SUV before going inside, according to the affidavit. Investigators say they went through Silva's phone and found months of text exchanges with a contact saved under the name Danilo Jaramillo, going back to August 17th. The affidavit says the messages followed a pattern, with Silva asking if Jaramillo was "available" and Jaramillo confirming before the two met up. Police say they used Silva's phone to text Jaramillo and arrange another deal. Jaramillo responded he could be there within the hour. Investigators say they followed Jaramillo's black Kia Telluride to Silva's apartment complex, then pulled him over. A K9 alerted to narcotics inside the vehicle. Investigators say they found a bag of fentanyl on the passenger seat, along with a large amount of cash. See also: Vero Beach animal hospital manager accused of reclaiming cats, abandoning them outside Detectives then obtained a search warrant for Jaramillo's home on SW Longfellow Road. According to a separate affidavit, investigators searched the master bedroom. They found three firearms a Smith & Wesson .40 caliber handgun, a Ruger LC9 and an AR-15 along with ammunition, digital scales, a written ledger, cocaine, marijuana and $17,715 in cash. Jaramillo's wife, Selina Jaramillo, was home with their children during the search. According to the affidavit, she told investigators she didn't know he was involved in drugs and said she'd last seen him with narcotics about eight months earlier. She said one of the firearms was hers, but that the rest, along with the drugs and cash, belonged to her husband. The affidavit says Jaramillo told police anything illegal in the home belonged to him, then asked for a lawyer before answering further questions. Because Jaramillo is a convicted felon, investigators charged him with three counts of possessing a firearm or ammunition as a felon. Police say body cameras were active throughout the search and the footage was submitted into evidence. Jaramillo, 43, faces multiple felony drug charges, including fentanyl trafficking, along with three felony weapons counts and a misdemeanor paraphernalia charge. He was booked into the St. Koch says oftentimes the pain is felt not just by the victims and dealers, but by the people around them. Many parents or family members feel guilty, like they didn't do enough or they couldn't. They say, "What could have been done differently?" So, they actually carry the guilt, Koch said. While state data points to a steady decline in overdose deaths since 2021, Koch says that addiction is still a rampant cycle. We're moving away from being in touch with who we are. We don't want to have any pain. We don't want to be bored. We want to be entertained. So these drugs come in, and who can compete with cocaine? CBS12 News has reached out to Port St. Lucie Police for comment and is working to confirm additional details.

entry.title: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Lucie fulfillment center is closing Thursday for a major renovation, leaving hundreds of workers out of a job while others have transferred to different facilities. When Amazon filed its layoff notice in July, 494 employees were listed as affected. Since then, more than 200 workers have transferred to other Amazon locations, according to information provided to CBS12 News. Around 300 employees are expected to take severance as the Port St. Lucie facility shuts down. Local workforce organizations, including CareerSource Research Coast and the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County, have spent recent months holding job fairs and helping affected workers connect with other employers. Lucie County Commissioner Cathy Townsend said the closure highlights the importance of attracting a wider range of businesses to the county. I think we need to be more strategic on the companies we want coming here, Townsend said. My focus would be more on small businesses. See also: CBS12 I-Team: Amendment 3 backers say tax relief could help Florida homeowners stay put The closure is expected to last until at least 2028. Amazon plans to invest about $200 million to renovate and expand the facility. Lucie EDC said the work will include advanced robotics and artificial intelligence capabilities, along with an additional 870,000 square feet. Amazon plans to reopen the facility in the second half of 2028 and hire more than 1,000 employees. Workers who were employed at the facility before the closure will be eligible for rehire when it reopens, according to the EDC. Amazon has said the closure is not expected to impact customers because operations will be handled by other facilities during the renovation.

entry.title: Dolphins rule out edge rusher Chop Robinson with a concussion for Week 2 at San Francisco
entry.summary: The Miami Dolphins ruled out edge rusher Chop Robinson ahead of their Week 2 matchup at San Francisco because of a concussion. Coach Jeff Hafley told reporters Friday at the team's training site in Napa, California, that Robinson sustained the concussion at practice this week. He was held out of practice Thursday. Robinson's absence Sunday could hurt a Dolphins' defense that struggled to stop the run and generate pressure against quarterback Kirk Cousins in their Week 1 loss to the Raiders. Cousins completed 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns, and running back Ashton Jeanty rushed for 102 yards on 23 attempts. Robinson suffered two concussions last season. The Dolphins are hoping for a leap from the third-year linebacker, who had a strong preseason but made just one tackle and struggled against the run in the season opener. The Dolphins at the end of the season will decide whether to pick up the fifth-year option on his rookie deal. Without Robinson, the Dolphins likely will turn to veteran Josh Uche and second-year defensive tackle Zeek Biggers. They also have Malik Herring, who signed with them a couple of weeks ago, and Clelin Ferrell, who is on the practice squad but was elevated to the active roster for the opener. We might do some other things to help out, but those guys I have confidence in,' Hafley said. 'They've been getting better. They all haven't been here for the entire time, but they've done a nice job in practice this week and it'll be the next man up.

entry.title: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Health officials have issued a blue-green algae health alert for an area of Lake Okeechobee after water samples detected harmful toxins. The Florida Department of Health in Martin County said the alert covers the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area and was issued in response to samples collected Sept. The area is located on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County. Residents and visitors should use caution in and around the lake, officials said. People should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials also advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water, according to the department. Officials said contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins. Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure, health officials said. RELATED: 'Influence campaign': Okeechobee County leaders want to change Lake O's narrative Officials said it is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903 . Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure to a harmful algae bloom can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222 . Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090 .

entry.article_text: A 42-year-old travel MRI technician was arrested after Port St. Lucie police said a patient reported she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI at HCA Florida St. Gabriel Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16 on a charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim, a first-degree felony, police said. Wasana Chesler is a former patient of St. Lucie Hospital and couldn't believe the news. That's very horrible," Chesler said. "That's very sad." The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before at the hospital, 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. Police said the woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy. Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital’s assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. See also: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police. Cruz had worked at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, police said. Monica Defoster said she's been to St. Lucie Hospital many times including on Thursday while visiting her husband. She calls the allegations disturbing. They should have more than one person in the MRI room," Defoster said. "You go to the hospital and don't expect something like that." The investigation remains active. Lucie Hospital has cooperated with investigators, police said. Lucie Hospital provided CBS12 News with the following statement: We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. When this serious allegation was reported to us, we contacted law enforcement and ended the individual’s assignment. We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient. A hospital spokesman told CBS12 no other complaints have been reported since Cruz stared working there late last month. Cruz's employer could not be reached for comment. He remains behind bars in Brevard County.

entry.title: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - cbs12.com
entry.summary: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis signed his 18th death warrant of the year Friday. William Reaves , convicted of the 1986 killing of an Indian River County Sheriff's deputy, is set to be executed by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Stark on Oct. According to court records, Reaves shot Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on September 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn’t have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, called the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After the deputy attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away from Raczkowski. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away, at which time Reaves fired four times into Raczkowski’s back. He would die a short time later. Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy as he was high on cocaine and panicked. Reaves was arrested three days later at a bus stop and charged with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. He entered a not guilty plea but was found guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987, with the jury giving a unanimous recommendation for the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor on the case who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury again found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, with the jury voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence. Florida leads the nation in executions, carrying out 15 of them this year after 19 were performed last year, the most in a single year by the state since the U.S. Supreme Court ended a four-year nationwide moratorium on capital punishment in 1976. Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a Polk County woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer in her home. Last Friday, DeSantis signed a warrant for William Lee Thompson, 74, to be executed Oct. 13 for the murder, kidnapping, and sexual battery of Sally Ivester more than 50 years ago in North Miami Beach. Counsel for Reaves quickly filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions for a stay they have also filed regarding Thompson are resolved. See also: Driver hits 120 mph on I-95 before crashing into tree, fence while fleeing FHP Both clients are due the best representation counsel can provide, particularly when both clients are facing a scheduled execution date, stated the motion from Reaves’ counsel Brittney Lacy. The state has conducted 43 executions under DeSantis, or 31 percent of the 140 carried out since 1976. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing for DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves as he is one that, in my opinion, should be a priority case. "It's very frustrating as the Sheriff, Flowers told WPEC last July. We want people to know that we're holding people accountable. And in this case, yes, he's jailed, yes, he's sitting there, but ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences. He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day.

This is causing the traffic to back up blocking the exit to the residents of Spinnaker Bay Dr. I have seen the police presence but parents are ignoring it" said the message.That tip led WPTV to Manatee Elementary School and the nearby Lake Charleston community.A mother named Michelle, who was picking up two of her children from school, said she understands why residents are frustrated."This is a pain in the butt if I lived in Lake Charleston," Michelle said. "It's a nightmare, it's a chaos of kids with a bunch of people loading right here and then some walking down here you never know what are crossing."Michelle said there are not enough places to park, but she chooses to park at a nearby approved county park and walk to the school because it takes about half as long as waiting in the traditional pick-up and drop-off line.She said the drop off look took her as long as two and a half hours, parking and walking took 15 minutes. "We support any and all improvements to improve local traffic flow, and our jurisdiction remains on School District property."The district also shared reminders sent to Manatee Elementary families, instructing parents to use the school's designated parent drop-off and pick-up loop off Hypoluxo Road. Families with students who walk or bike are encouraged to use the county park parking lot next door to campus and access the school's east-side biker and walker entrance.The district also warned families not to use the nearby Public Storage facility as a parking or drop-off location."Please refrain from using the Public Storage facility (behind the Winn Dixie plaza) as a parking space or drop off location in the morning," the message states. entry.summary: Florida governor signs death warrant for William Reaves Jr., convicted of killing Indian River County deputy    WPTV
entry.article_text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has signed a death warrant for 77-year-old William Reaves Jr., the man convicted of murdering Indian River County Sheriff's Deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The execution is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. 20, at 6 p.m.WATCH BELOW: Man who killed Indian River Co. deputy to be executed in OctoberReaves was convicted of murdereing Raczkoski on Sept. 23, 1986, after a confrontation at a convenience store.Deputy Raczkoski had responded to a 911 call at the store when he encountered Reaves. During a conversation between the two, a gun fell from Reaves's shorts. Deputy Raczkoski placed his knee on the weapon. Reaves then pushed the deputy away, grabbed the gun and pointed it at Deputy Raczkoski's face.As Deputy Raczkoski attempted to draw his own weapon, Reaves said, "I wouldn't do that if I were you." The deputy backed away, turned, and ran. Reaves fired seven rounds, striking Deputy Raczkoski four times.Reaves was tried in the 19th Judicial Circuit in Indian River County. On direct appeal, the Florida Supreme Court reversed the initial conviction and remanded the case for a new trial. On remand, Reaves was again convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on March 6, 1992, in Vero Beach.The Florida Supreme Court affirmed the conviction and death sentence on April 7, 1994. The United States Supreme Court denied Reaves's petition for a writ of certiorari on Nov. 7, 1994.Reaves pursued numerous postconviction challenges in both state and federal courts over the following decades.In 2015, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida granted Reaves's federal petition for a writ of habeas corpus. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit overturned that ruling and ordered that the petition be denied.Additional postconviction motions and petitions were subsequently denied, and those denials were affirmed on appeal. Executive clemency was also considered and denied.Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, in his letter recommending the warrant, wrote that "the record is legally sufficient to support the issuance of a death warrant," and confirmed that "there are no stays of execution issued by any court of competent jurisdiction in this cause."The execution is scheduled to take place at Florida State Prison in Raiford. If carried out as scheduled, it will come 40 years after the murder of Deputy Raczkoski.

Florida Senate’s fiscal analysis here.Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd offered a blunt assessment."911, what is your emergency? It's a train wreck," Judd said.The St. Pete Polls survey contacted 913 likely voters Sept. 15-17 and reported a margin of error of 3.2 percentage points. Its question described Amendment 3 as eliminating non-school property taxes on homesteaded residences, language broader than the scheduled exemption increases. Survey details here.Voters will decide the amendment Nov.

entry.title: Health alert issued for Boca Raton waterways after wastewater spill near Intracoastal
entry.summary: A health alert, no-swim advisory and no-irrigation advisory has been issued for waterways near the Boca Raton Resort following a wastewater spill into Camino Real, connected to the Intracoastal Waterway just northwest of the resort, the Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach County announced Friday afternoon. The department said drinking water is not affected. The city of Boca Raton is coordinating testing and cleanup actions with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection, health officials said. Until further information is known regarding possible bacterial contamination, residents and visitors in the area are urged to take precautions when in contact with the affected waterways, the department said. Health officials are urging anyone who comes into contact with the water in the area to wash thoroughly, especially before eating or drinking, as water contaminated with high levels of fecal bacteria can cause disease, infections or rashes. Sensitive individuals, including children, the elderly and those who are immunocompromised, may still be at risk even at low concentrations and should avoid any exposure. For more information about the potential health effects of wastewater overflow, contact the Florida Department of Health in Palm Beach County at 561-837-5900 or CHD50ContactUs@FLHealth.gov . For after-hours questions or inquiries, call 561-881-1888.

"I'm afraid it's going to come up through the foundation."As residents dealt with flooding, crews with the Indian Trail Improvement District worked around the clock to manage water levels, monitor canals and respond to reports of breaches and drainage problems.Elizabeth Accomando with the district said crews prepared the system before the storm and lowered canal levels where possible."Our canals were very low in most cases," Accomando said. But she said the sheer volume and intensity of the rainfall overwhelmed the system."If you think about how water works and how water drains, first of all, no matter how much you pump, if it's coming down just as fast or as much in volume, we can't pump out that fast," she said.Accomando said the district operates at the "head" of a larger interconnected drainage network that includes Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, Palm Beach County and the South Florida Water Management District."As we're discharging the water, which we have been, it has to flow downhill," she said. "So we have to wait for everybody at the bottom end to get drained out before we can drain." The South Florida Water Management District said its regional flood control system is operating normally and has capacity for expected weekend rainfall.In a statement, the agency said the regional system includes more than 2,300 miles of canals and 2,200 miles of berms and levees that move water from local drainage districts and municipalities.The district said it is aware of complaints involving flooding along the M Canal, which it said is not operated or maintained by South Florida Water Management. Water from that canal flows into the district-operated C-51 Canal, which officials said is currently moving stormwater from western Palm Beach County."The District's regional flood control system throughout its 16-county area of responsibility is ready for any rainfall expected this weekend and no problems have been reported with the District's flood control infrastructure," the statement said.Accomando said crews have been in the field continuously, although lightning has temporarily slowed operations."Every single person is out working, but when it's lightning, they have got to go into their trucks," she said. "They can't be out moving water in the middle of a lightning storm."The district said it has also been inundated with calls from residents seeking answers and assistance. "We have 50,000 residents, and if everybody's calling at once, it's impossible," Accomando said. "But we are paying attention."The district brought in additional staff to answer calls, emails and voicemails while field crews continued working flooded areas.Officials said the recent drought also contributed to the flooding. Accomando described current conditions as part of a "75-year drought," which left the ground compacted and less able to absorb sudden heavy rainfall."When the rain does come, it's going to be a deluge," she said. "So this is like the new normal."Some residents questioned why canals were not lowered further before the storm, but Accomando said aggressively draining canals during drought conditions can create additional problems, including unstable canal banks."Swales and canals are technically designed to hold the water until we can get it out of the district," she said. "Now we've gotten so much rain so fast that there's nothing that can hold that much water at once."Officials are urging residents not to drive through standing water and to help by clearing swales, culverts and drains near their homes."With more than 400 miles of roads and thousands of miles of canals and swales to monitor, we need residents to be our eyes," Accomando said.Despite residents' frustration and fears, district leaders said crews will continue working through the weekend as more rain remains possible.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 41-year-old man holding shotgun fatally shot by Sebastian police
entry.summary: Two Sebastian officers are on administrative leave after police said they fatally shot a 41-year-old man, who was armed with a shotgun, Thursday night. During Friday morning news conference, interim police Chief Tim Wood said the situation began at about 9:25 p.m. when officers arrived at a home in the 500 block of Joy Haven Drive for a noise complaint. WATCH BELOW: Man with shotgun fatally shot by Sebastian police 41-year-old man with shotgun fatally shot by police in Sebastian Police said after officers arrived, they made contact with the suspect's mother. While they were speaking with her, Wood said officers could hear a man, later identified as Keaton Daucher, 41, yelling inside the home. Wood said Daucher then came out of the home with a shotgun, prompting the two officers to discharge their weapons, killing him. Police said it was unclear if Daucher, who lived at the home, pointed the shotgun at the officers or if he fired any shots. Police said that law enforcement had previously been at the house before Thursday, however it was unclear how many times. WATCH BELOW: Police hold news conference on officer-involved shooting The agency said that the investigation remains ongoing and has been turned over to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which is standard practice for their agency. Neither of the officers were hurt and both have been placed on paid administrative leave pending the investigation, police said.

entry.title: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs - WPEC
entry.summary: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie fulfillment center is closing Thursday for a major renovation, leaving hundreds of workers out of a job while others have transferred to different facilities. When Amazon filed its layoff notice in July, 494 employees were listed as affected. Since then, more than 200 workers have transferred to other Amazon locations, according to information provided to CBS12 News. Around 300 employees are expected to take severance as the Port St. Lucie facility shuts down. Local workforce organizations, including CareerSource Research Coast and the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County, have spent recent months holding job fairs and helping affected workers connect with other employers. Lucie County Commissioner Cathy Townsend said the closure highlights the importance of attracting a wider range of businesses to the county. I think we need to be more strategic on the companies we want coming here, Townsend said. My focus would be more on small businesses. See also: CBS12 I-Team: Amendment 3 backers say tax relief could help Florida homeowners stay put The closure is expected to last until at least 2028. Amazon plans to invest about $200 million to renovate and expand the facility. Lucie EDC said the work will include advanced robotics and artificial intelligence capabilities, along with an additional 870,000 square feet. Amazon plans to reopen the facility in the second half of 2028 and hire more than 1,000 employees. Workers who were employed at the facility before the closure will be eligible for rehire when it reopens, according to the EDC. Amazon has said the closure is not expected to impact customers because operations will be handled by other facilities during the renovation.

entry.title: Florida governor signs death warrant for William Reaves Jr., convicted of killing Indian River County deputy - WFLX
entry.summary: Florida governor signs death warrant for William Reaves Jr., convicted of killing Indian River County deputy    WFLX
entry.article_text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has signed a death warrant for 77-year-old William Reaves Jr., the man convicted of murdering Indian River County Sheriff’s Deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The execution is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. Reaves was convicted of murdereing Raczkoski on Sept. 23, 1986, after a confrontation at a convenience store. Deputy Raczkoski had responded to a 911 call at the store when he encountered Reaves. During a conversation between the two, a gun fell from Reaves’s shorts. Deputy Raczkoski placed his knee on the weapon. Reaves then pushed the deputy away, grabbed the gun and pointed it at Deputy Raczkoski’s face. As Deputy Raczkoski attempted to draw his own weapon, Reaves said, “I wouldn’t do that if I were you.” The deputy backed away, turned, and ran. Reaves fired seven rounds, striking Deputy Raczkoski four times. Reaves was tried in the 19th Judicial Circuit in Indian River County. On direct appeal, the Florida Supreme Court reversed the initial conviction and remanded the case for a new trial. On remand, Reaves was again convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on March 6, 1992, in Vero Beach. The Florida Supreme Court affirmed the conviction and death sentence on April 7, 1994. The United States Supreme Court denied Reaves’s petition for a writ of certiorari on Nov. Reaves pursued numerous postconviction challenges in both state and federal courts over the following decades. District Court for the Southern District of Florida granted Reaves’s federal petition for a writ of habeas corpus. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit overturned that ruling and ordered that the petition be denied. Additional postconviction motions and petitions were subsequently denied, and those denials were affirmed on appeal. Executive clemency was also considered and denied. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, in his letter recommending the warrant, wrote that “the record is legally sufficient to support the issuance of a death warrant,” and confirmed that “there are no stays of execution issued by any court of competent jurisdiction in this cause.” The execution is scheduled to take place at Florida State Prison in Raiford. If carried out as scheduled, it will come 40 years after the murder of Deputy Raczkoski.

entry.summary: Operation Late Checkout targets human trafficking in Indian River County    WPBF
entry.article_text: Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers Thursday that law enforcement had made 50 arrests as the result of a four-day operation called Operation Late Checkout. "This was an operation with a targeted goal of stopping human trafficking," Flowers said. Flowers said they were specifically targeting the trafficking of children. "Working to capture people who are trying to lure children on the internet and meet up with those children," Flowers said. "This operation shows that within our communities, there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," said Special Agent Alphonso Williams, of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. Authorities pointed to cases like that of Carlos Reyes-Ayala, who is accused of traveling to Indian River County to meet with a child for sex. Flowers said investigators connected with many others seeking to exploit children. "We had a whole roomful of detectives that were chatting undercover with people who wanted to meet up with children. Our team was busy for days," Flowers said. Operation Late Checkout involved local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. In total, 50 arrests were made, nearly all for prostitution. Authorities also said they identified multiple individuals they believe are victims of human trafficking, and those investigations are ongoing. It hurts our hearts when we see these cases and we see these kids. So, that's why we do these things," Flowers said. Flowers said he expects more arrests to happen as a result of Operation Late Checkout. entry.summary: Martin County High School receives third bomb threat in eight days    WPBF
entry.article_text: Martin County High School received another threat through the state's FortifyFL reporting system, the third bomb threat involving our campus this week, the school district said Friday afternoon. "I recognize that you have heard from me repeatedly this week regarding safety-related disruptions on our campus," Principal Lori Vogel said in a message to families. The latest threat referenced two specific buildings, requiring students and staff to be evacuated while law enforcement conducted a thorough search. Students and staff were relocated to other areas of campus during the response. On Monday, students and staff were evacuated after a bomb threat prompted a response from the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Eight days ago, students and staff were evacuated in the afternoon after a bomb threat was received via email, according to school officials. In a message sent to families, school officials said all buildings were being evacuated at the direction of law enforcement while authorities investigate the threat. Vogel noted the seriousness of the threats. "Every threat must be taken seriously," the principal said. "Each report generates a significant law enforcement response, disrupts instruction, displaces students and staff, and creates understandable concern throughout our school community. Unlike many situations that may require an emergency response, the behavior prompting these repeated disruptions is entirely avoidable. We need our families as partners in addressing this behavior. Please speak directly with your children about the seriousness and far-reaching impact of making or participating in a false threat." The message added: "What a student may view as a joke or a temporary way to avoid class can have widespread consequences for an entire campus and community. FortifyFL is an important safety resource. Students and families who become aware of a credible threat—or who have a legitimate reason to believe questionable, dangerous or criminal activity may be occurring—should continue to report that information through FortifyFL. Information about submitting a report is available on our school's and the School District's websites. "However, FortifyFL must never be used to submit information that someone knows to be false," the message said. "The District has zero tolerance for anyone who knowingly misuses the platform or participates in making a false threat. Any individual found responsible will face severe school disciplinary consequences and potential criminal charges." The principal concluded: "We appreciate your partnership in reinforcing that false threats are neither harmless nor funny. They place an unacceptable burden on students, employees, families, law enforcement and the broader community—and they must stop. Thank you for your immediate attention to this serious matter and for partnering with us to maintain a safe, orderly learning environment for every student and staff member at Martin County High School." entry.title: Former NYPD officer who worked Ground Zero now leads Martin County school safety - WPTV
entry.summary: Former NYPD officer who worked Ground Zero now leads Martin County school safety    WPTV
entry.article_text: Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, Frank Frangella still carries the memories of what he witnessed at Ground Zero. The Martin County School District's Director of Safety & Security was a New York City Police Department officer when terrorists struck the World Trade Center on Sept. 11, 2001.WATCH BELOW:"It's always there and there are always little things that remind you of what happened," Frangella said from his office, surrounded by photos, statues and a book of memories honoring those lost in the attacks.Frangella was asleep after working the midnight shift when his wife woke him with news that would change his life forever."I was actually asleep when the first plane hit and my wife woke me up and she goes – a plane just hit the World Trade Center," Frangella recalled. "There was a big hole in that building and I knew right away what that was, so I just started dressing."The weather that morning remains etched in his memory. "The one thing I remember from that day, soon as I walked out of the house – it was the most beautiful day in the world. There wasn't a cloud in the sky, and I'm thinking to myself driving to where I was going – how can this happen on such a beautiful day."Initially assigned to help intake victims at a Staten Island triage area, Frangella waited for hours as no injured survivors arrived. "It was like what's happening, you know. We're not getting any information."With communication systems failing, Frangella and fellow officers decided to take a boat directly to Ground Zero. What they found defied comprehension."By that time, both buildings were down. And I mean - it looked like a war zone," he said. "It was literally a pile, and it was huge."The scale of destruction was unlike anything Frangella had ever seen. "You figure two of the largest buildings in Manhattan, you didn't see a desk. Nothing that resembled an office building," he said. "Everything was pulverized."SPECIAL COVERAGE: Remembering 9/11What began as a rescue mission quickly became a recovery operation, according to Frangella. "Everybody that was down there was doing it because they wanted to save lives, and then we found out pretty quickly on that there was no lives to save, and it was a recovery mission more than anything else."Despite their efforts, Frangella's team did not find any survivors.The emotional toll of those days followed Frangella home to his family. "A few weeks later, I remember sitting home and it all hit. I just started crying and I don't even know why I was crying," he said.The dust-covered uniforms from Ground Zero created an unexpected memorial in the Frangella household. "We had a washing machine in the basement that she was washing all my clothing with and how many souls were in that wash. So, it was almost like a shrine in my house. We never used it again after 9/11 because it was like – it just felt wrong to use it."Today, Frangella applies his experience from that tragic day to his role protecting Martin County's school children. He often shares his story with students, creating powerful moments of connection."This little girl about this big walks over to me and she says -- can I hug you? When that little girl came over, there wasn't a dry eye in the house. I mean everybody started crying and she just said… thank you. It was the most amazing thing in the world," Frangella said.Despite his role in the response efforts, Frangella has never visited the 9/11 Memorial and Museum. "I was there when it happened. I don't need to relive it again," he said.As the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks approaches, first responders like Frangella continue processing their experiences while serving their communities in new ways. His transition from protecting New York City to safeguarding Martin County schools demonstrates how the impact of that day continues to shape public service careers across the country.Twenty-five years later, Frangella honors not just his own experience, but that of every person who responded that day. "There are thousands upon thousands of stories. This is just mine," he said. "Everybody says that time heals all, and I know for me and everybody who was down there -- we're still waiting."To hear more stories be sure to watch Echoes of September: A 9/11 Special on Friday, Sept. on WPTVThis story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WFLX
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday. Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. “Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” Flowers said. The operation’s targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff’s office said. During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. “Our team did a great job of getting him off the street,” Flowers said. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff’s office said. Victims’ advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. “We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this,” Flowers said. Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. “We’ve never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot,” he said. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. “This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it,” Williams said. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. “Our work is far from done,” Williams said. “This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today.” FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. entry.title: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee - WPEC
entry.summary: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee    WPEC
entry.article_text: Health officials have issued a blue-green algae health alert for an area of Lake Okeechobee after water samples detected harmful toxins. The Florida Department of Health in Martin County said the alert covers the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area and was issued in response to samples collected Sept. The area is located on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County. Residents and visitors should use caution in and around the lake, officials said. People should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials also advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water, according to the department. Officials said contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins. Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure, health officials said. RELATED: 'Influence campaign': Okeechobee County leaders want to change Lake O's narrative Officials said it is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903 . Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure to a harmful algae bloom can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222 . Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090 .

entry.title: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning in Hobe Sound despite some data center concerns - WFLX
entry.summary: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning in Hobe Sound despite some data center concerns    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Martin County Commission approved a zoning compromise for land in Hobe Sound, but the 3-2 vote has left some residents and at least one commissioner with lingering concerns about what could be built there. Commissioners voted to rezone a property along Southeast Powerline Avenue to limited-industrial, stepping back from a general industrial designation that drew pushback from nearby residents. The property has long been slated for some form of industrial use, but the county said the existing zoning was outdated and due for an update. WATCH: Hobe Sound zoning compromise raises data center concerns Residents who spoke at the Tuesday commission meeting said their primary concern was protecting the character of the community. Steve Addison said he has lived in the area since 1969. “Our biggest concern was preserving our quality of life. We don’t have a lot of industry and a lot of noise,” Addison said. Other residents echoed concerns about the scope of the original rezoning proposal. “I understand that Martin County has to plan for the future but I also believe that growth needs to be compatible with the community that already exists,” Kim Call, a resident, said. “We’re concerned about the permanence of a GI classification which we believe is too broad and too open-ended,” Patrick McDonough, a Hobe Sound resident and Eaglewood Community HOA president, said. After hearing from residents, the property owner offered to accept the less-intensive classification. “To cooperate and show if that’s what the neighbors feel is more appropriate and that would be a better use then we are willing to accept the light industrial,” Bob Reins, a land-use attorney with Gunster law firm, said. Despite the compromise, Commissioner Blake Capps voted against the rezoning, citing concerns about the potential for a data center on the site. “Who knows where this is really going in the future and to approve a zoning for this property that allows a data center. I’m not into that,” Capps said. The county said there are no plans for a data center at the site. Any proposal exceeding 100,000 square feet would require board approval. In speaking with residents, WPTV’S Cassandra Garcia learned not everyone was happy with the outcome. However, residents like Addison felt it was the right move. “I don’t want to see over development, but I also don’t want to be that guy that doesn’t understand land-use and doesn’t understand property rights,” Addison said. “I feel like it was a win win for the both of us.” This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.summary: 'Just heard like two big pop pops': Two men arrested after road rage shooting in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two men were arrested after a road rage incident escalated into a shooting near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. Neighbors reported hearing gunfire at approximately 6:30 p.m. "OK, last night we were trying to put the kids down, and we just heard like two big pop pops," resident Ripley Crawford said. "All we saw was the cars were kind of already pulled to the side, and you could see there was like a crash of sorts." The Port St. Lucie Police Department determined the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between two drivers following a lane change and merging near Southwest Crosstown Parkway. One driver believed he was being followed after the vehicles crossed paths, but investigators found no intentional following. One of the drivers, 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, was traveling with his girlfriend to her home after visiting a local restaurant. The other driver, 41-year-old Dean Plotts, happened to be traveling in the same direction and onto the same streets. As the vehicles continued, the situation escalated into a physical confrontation near SW Brevity Terrace. During the altercation, Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office deputy traveling on SW California Boulevard observed the incident and detained Kukielka. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Later that night, traffic was rerouted as investigators gathered evidence at the scene. "The traffic was just nonstop because they closed California. My neighbor got a call from her daughter in Tennessee that said there was a shooting down here," resident Ernie Lampreda said. Plotts sustained gunshot wounds to his left wrist and legs and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also transported for medical evaluation. Detectives responded to the scene and collected evidence, including shell casings, surveillance video, and dash cam footage that captured portions of the incident. Based on the evidence, witness information, and statements obtained during the investigation, detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Kukielka with attempted homicide – murder, dangerous depraved without premeditation, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 782.04(2). Detectives also determined there was probable cause to charge Plotts with burglary with assault or battery, a felony under Florida Statute 810.02(2)(a). Both men were taken into custody, and the investigation remains ongoing. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions    WPBF
entry.article_text: A Fort Pierce man was arrested after a raid Friday by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and U.S. Marshals Service found a massive amount of illicit drugs, including fentanyl and cocaine, worth several million dollars. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office Special Investigations Division, with assistance from the SWAT Team and the U.S. Marshals Service, executed a narcotics-related search warrant at a residence in the 3100 block of S. 24th Street in Fort Pierce. The subject of the investigation, Tony Saunders, 48, was taken into custody. Saunders, a three-time convicted felon who is on federal probation, also had two active warrants related to the sale and delivery of controlled substances. Afterward, Saunders faced additional charges of trafficking in fentanyl, trafficking in cocaine, trafficking in MDPV, manufacturing cocaine, tampering with evidence and possession of marijuana with intent to sell. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0j4igLYhtX4QpfPCZhHkYeREcfiqd9eehsAoAcjVwDWTipnXHZNWyrJLe6gbwukcvl The search resulted in the seizure of approximately 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl, 303 grams of cocaine, 97 grams of marijuana laced with MDPV, and 60 oxycodone pills totaling approximately 6.2 grams, the sheriff's office said. The street value of 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl can range from $150,000 to nearly $1.8 million, depending heavily on its purity, geographic location, and whether it is sold as wholesale powder or broken down into counterfeit pills, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection. The estimated street value of 303 grams of cocaine in the U.S. ranges between roughly $18,180 and $60,600. Detectives also seized assorted ammunition, drug paraphernalia and materials consistent with the preparation and distribution of narcotics. A single kilogram of fentanyl has the potential to kill 500,000 people, making 4.5 kilograms a lethal volume capable of millions of fatal doses, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. “4.5 kilos of fentanyl are 4.5 kilos that will not reach our streets," Sheriff Richard Del Tro said. "Fentanyl is a deadly poison, and those who traffic in it are putting lives at risk for profit. I commend our detectives, SWAT Team, and the U.S. Marshals Service for their commitment to this mission. We will continue to pursue those who traffic dangerous narcotics and do everything within our authority to make St. Lucie County the safest county in Florida.” Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25
