entry.summary: Port St. Lucie hospital MRI technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 42-year-old travel MRI technician was arrested after Port St. Lucie police said a patient reported she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI at HCA Florida St. Gabriel Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16 on a charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim, a first-degree felony, police said. Wasana Chesler is a former patient of St. Lucie Hospital and couldn't believe the news. That's very horrible," Chesler said. "That's very sad." The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before at the hospital, 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. Police said the woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy. Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital’s assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. See also: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police. Cruz had worked at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, police said. Monica Defoster said she's been to St. Lucie Hospital many times including on Thursday while visiting her husband. She calls the allegations disturbing. They should have more than one person in the MRI room," Defoster said. "You go to the hospital and don't expect something like that." The investigation remains active. Lucie Hospital has cooperated with investigators, police said. Lucie Hospital provided CBS12 News with the following statement: We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. When this serious allegation was reported to us, we contacted law enforcement and ended the individual’s assignment. We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient. A hospital spokesman told CBS12 no other complaints have been reported since Cruz stared working there late last month. Cruz's employer could not be reached for comment. He remains behind bars in Brevard County.

entry.title: Execution date set for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - WPBF
entry.summary: Execution date set for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    WPBF
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis has set a date for the execution of the man who killed an Indian River County sheriff's deputy nearly 40 years ago. In September 1986, William Reaves shot Deputy Richard Raczkoski four times at a convenience store near Vero Beach. On Friday morning, DeSantis signed the death warrant for Reaves. I've been saying that all day. It's been a great Friday in Indian River County," Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said. Flowers never met Raczkoski. He was only 6 years old when Raczkoski was killed. But he said people still talk all the time about the man everybody knew as "Raz." "The stories that I hear are just that he was one of the best guys that we had around. He was known for having his hairbrush in his car," Flowers said. To ensure Raczkoski's legacy lives on, Flowers added a 1986 patrol car, Raz's car, to the department a few years ago. "We want people to remember that he made the ultimate sacrifice, that all of us are here today in his memory. All of us are here serving our community in the same way that he did. And it's important to never forget," Flowers said. Flowers said that's why he's been so vocal for years about wanting the death penalty for Reaves and why it meant so much when the governor's office called him Friday morning to inform him that the death warrant had been signed. It's something that's been weighing on us. You know, next week is 40 years," Flowers said. Forty years of appeals and a retrial, all resulting in the same outcome: a death sentence. The execution is scheduled for Oct. 27, a fact Flowers shared with everyone. "It was an honor to be able to make all the phone calls that came in the wake of that, to call our retirees, to call his son," Flowers said. Raczkoski's son never met his father. He was born shortly after Raczkoski was killed. Now, he knows the man responsible for murdering his father will face the death penalty. "Raz never got to see his son. And this guy has just been wasting our taxpayer dollars for the last 40 years up there. It's time to get this over with," Flowers said. Flowers said he plans to attend the execution, ensuring the last thing Reaves sees is an Indian River County sheriff's uniform as a reminder of what he did. entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WFLX
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WFLX
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county. Operation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday. Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement. “Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office, Seminole County Sheriff’s Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” Flowers said. The operation’s targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff’s office said. During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time. One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online. “Our team did a great job of getting him off the street,” Flowers said. Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff’s office said. Victims’ advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked. “We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this,” Flowers said. Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County. “We’ve never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot,” he said. FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county. “This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it,” Williams said. Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors. “Our work is far from done,” Williams said. “This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today.” FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the hotline at 1-855-352-7233. READ OPERATION LATE CHECKOUT BELOW:

entry.title: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning in Hobe Sound despite some data center concerns - wflx.com
entry.summary: Martin County approves limited-industrial zoning in Hobe Sound despite some data center concerns    wflx.com
entry.article_text: The Martin County Commission approved a zoning compromise for land in Hobe Sound, but the 3-2 vote has left some residents and at least one commissioner with lingering concerns about what could be built there. Commissioners voted to rezone a property along Southeast Powerline Avenue to limited-industrial, stepping back from a general industrial designation that drew pushback from nearby residents. The property has long been slated for some form of industrial use, but the county said the existing zoning was outdated and due for an update. WATCH: Hobe Sound zoning compromise raises data center concerns Residents who spoke at the Tuesday commission meeting said their primary concern was protecting the character of the community. Steve Addison said he has lived in the area since 1969. “Our biggest concern was preserving our quality of life. We don’t have a lot of industry and a lot of noise,” Addison said. Other residents echoed concerns about the scope of the original rezoning proposal. “I understand that Martin County has to plan for the future but I also believe that growth needs to be compatible with the community that already exists,” Kim Call, a resident, said. “We’re concerned about the permanence of a GI classification which we believe is too broad and too open-ended,” Patrick McDonough, a Hobe Sound resident and Eaglewood Community HOA president, said. After hearing from residents, the property owner offered to accept the less-intensive classification. “To cooperate and show if that’s what the neighbors feel is more appropriate and that would be a better use then we are willing to accept the light industrial,” Bob Reins, a land-use attorney with Gunster law firm, said. Despite the compromise, Commissioner Blake Capps voted against the rezoning, citing concerns about the potential for a data center on the site. “Who knows where this is really going in the future and to approve a zoning for this property that allows a data center. I’m not into that,” Capps said. The county said there are no plans for a data center at the site. Any proposal exceeding 100,000 square feet would require board approval. In speaking with residents, WPTV’S Cassandra Garcia learned not everyone was happy with the outcome. However, residents like Addison felt it was the right move. “I don’t want to see over development, but I also don’t want to be that guy that doesn’t understand land-use and doesn’t understand property rights,” Addison said. “I feel like it was a win win for the both of us.” This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: Flooding swamps the Acreage as more rain threatens the area this weekend
entry.summary: Crews are working to pump water out of flooded streets and yards in the Acreage as the area braces for more rain this weekend, following more than 9 inches of rainfall Thursday. More heavy rain hit the area Saturday, compounding the flooding that has left roads, swales and canals overflowing throughout the neighborhood. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: Flooding swamps the Acreage as more rain threatens the area this weekend Resident Arlene Rodriguez described the situation around her home as a moat. 'We left yesterday at around 11/11:30 and we still had a driveway and we came home at 2/2:30 and we were underwater. It was just insane,' Rodriguez said. Rodriguez said water in her front yard reached as much as 10 inches deep in some areas. 'It's a lot of rain really fast,' Rodriguez said. Neighbor Erik Mack said the flooding made it impossible to use his driveway. 'I can't get in and out of the driveway with the vehicles,' Mack said. Mack said he found a workaround while crews respond. 'I have to take the golf cart to come in, in and out and park the cars out front here,' Mack said. Cleanup efforts have been slowed by lightning delays, forcing crews to pause work and shelter in their trucks. 'Every single person is out working, but when it's lightning, they have got to go into their trucks,' Elizabeth Accomando of the Indian Trail Improvement District said. While Mack said he was glad to see crews responding, he believes a different approach could have prevented some of the damage. 'There's culverts under here and they all get blocked so if they do stuff like that. They don't have to worry about doing it after the fact,' Mack said. Rodriguez said the flooding has spread well beyond her property. 'There's just water everywhere. It's just everywhere I go the streets are flooded,' Rodriguez said. Despite the conditions, Rodriguez said her home has so far avoided the worst of it though she remains anxious about what is still to come. 'As long as it's not coming up to the door. We're okay right now, but there's more rain in the forecast and hopefully it stays where it is,' Rodriguez said. The South Florida Water Management District said drains have capacity and water is moving, indicating the system is ready for any additional rain this weekend. entry.title: Two men arrested after road rage incident leads to shooting in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: Two men arrested after road rage incident leads to shooting in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two men were arrested after a road rage incident escalated into a shooting near SW California Boulevard and SW Brevity Terrace on Sept. 17, 2026, at approximately 6:30 p.m., according to the Port St. Investigators determined the incident began as a misunderstanding between two drivers. One driver believed he was being followed after changing lanes and merging from SW Crosstown Parkway, where the vehicles had crossed paths, and one driver thought the other had cut him off. However, police said the investigation revealed there was no intentional following. One of the drivers, identified as 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, was traveling with his girlfriend to her home after visiting a local restaurant. The other driver, identified as 41-year-old Dean Plotts, happened to be traveling in the same direction and onto the same streets. As the vehicles continued, the situation escalated into a physical confrontation near SW Brevity Terrace. During the altercation, Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Lucie County Sheriff's Office deputy who was in the area traveling on SW California Boulevard observed the incident and detained Kukielka. Plotts sustained gunshot wounds to his left wrist and legs and was transported to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also transported for medical evaluation. Detectives responded to the scene and collected evidence, including shell casings, surveillance video, dash cam footage, and other physical evidence. Based on the evidence collected, witness information, video footage, and statements obtained during the investigation, detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Kukielka with attempted homicide – murder, dangerous depraved without premeditation, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 782.04(2). Detectives also determined there was probable cause to charge Plotts with burglary with assault or battery, a felony under Florida Statute 810.02(2)(a). Both men were taken into custody in connection with the investigation, which remains ongoing. All defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in a court of law. entry.article_text: A man has been sentenced to 10 years behind bars for his role in a 2024 Vero Beach shooting. According to the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office , Vandrell Jacobs, 25, was arrested on Jan. 29, 2024 following an investigation into an Indian River County shooting that took place the day prior. IRCSO says that deputies responded to reports of gunfire at the Orangewood Apartments in Vero Beach on Jan. Investigators said five bullets struck an apartment occupied by a family, and witnesses reported seeing people inside a red Mercedes firing shots towards an intended victim before fleeing. Surveillance footage shows the Mercedes stopping in the area of the shooting before driving away, and IRCSO says that Flock cameras recorded the car for about two minutes before the shooting. See also: Sebastian Police identify man killed in officer-involved shooting; FDLE investigating A deputy who responded to the shooting pursued the Mercedes, but the car fled at a high speed and ran red lights. The following day, the Mercedes was located and Jacobs was arrested. At the time, he admitted to the allegations, and was charged with shooting into a dwelling/vehicle/building and fleeing police with disregard for safety. Now, he begins a decade-long prison sentence.

entry.title: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - cbs12.com
entry.summary: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis signed his 18th death warrant of the year Friday. William Reaves , convicted of the 1986 killing of an Indian River County Sheriff's deputy, is set to be executed by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Stark on Oct. According to court records, Reaves shot Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on September 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn’t have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, called the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After the deputy attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away from Raczkowski. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away, at which time Reaves fired four times into Raczkowski’s back. He would die a short time later. Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy as he was high on cocaine and panicked. Reaves was arrested three days later at a bus stop and charged with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. He entered a not guilty plea but was found guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987, with the jury giving a unanimous recommendation for the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor on the case who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury again found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, with the jury voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence. Florida leads the nation in executions, carrying out 15 of them this year after 19 were performed last year, the most in a single year by the state since the U.S. Supreme Court ended a four-year nationwide moratorium on capital punishment in 1976. Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a Polk County woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer in her home. Last Friday, DeSantis signed a warrant for William Lee Thompson, 74, to be executed Oct. 13 for the murder, kidnapping, and sexual battery of Sally Ivester more than 50 years ago in North Miami Beach. Counsel for Reaves quickly filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions for a stay they have also filed regarding Thompson are resolved. See also: Driver hits 120 mph on I-95 before crashing into tree, fence while fleeing FHP Both clients are due the best representation counsel can provide, particularly when both clients are facing a scheduled execution date, stated the motion from Reaves’ counsel Brittney Lacy. The state has conducted 43 executions under DeSantis, or 31 percent of the 140 carried out since 1976. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing for DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves as he is one that, in my opinion, should be a priority case. "It's very frustrating as the Sheriff, Flowers told WPEC last July. We want people to know that we're holding people accountable. And in this case, yes, he's jailed, yes, he's sitting there, but ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences. He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie hospital MRI technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie hospital MRI technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: A 42-year-old travel MRI technician was arrested after Port St. Lucie police said a patient reported she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI at HCA Florida St. Gabriel Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16 on a charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim, a first-degree felony, police said. Wasana Chesler is a former patient of St. Lucie Hospital and couldn't believe the news. That's very horrible," Chesler said. "That's very sad." The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before at the hospital, 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. Police said the woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy. Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital’s assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. See also: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police. Cruz had worked at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, police said. Monica Defoster said she's been to St. Lucie Hospital many times including on Thursday while visiting her husband. She calls the allegations disturbing. They should have more than one person in the MRI room," Defoster said. "You go to the hospital and don't expect something like that." The investigation remains active. Lucie Hospital has cooperated with investigators, police said. Lucie Hospital provided CBS12 News with the following statement: We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. When this serious allegation was reported to us, we contacted law enforcement and ended the individual’s assignment. We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient. A hospital spokesman told CBS12 no other complaints have been reported since Cruz stared working there late last month. Cruz's employer could not be reached for comment. He remains behind bars in Brevard County.

entry.title: 41-year-old man holding shotgun fatally shot by Sebastian police
entry.summary: Two Sebastian officers are on administrative leave after police said they fatally shot a 41-year-old man, who was armed with a shotgun, Thursday night. During Friday morning news conference, interim police Chief Tim Wood said the situation began at about 9:25 p.m. when officers arrived at a home in the 500 block of Joy Haven Drive for a noise complaint. WATCH BELOW: Man with shotgun fatally shot by Sebastian police 41-year-old man with shotgun fatally shot by police in Sebastian Police said after officers arrived, they made contact with the suspect's mother. While they were speaking with her, Wood said officers could hear a man, later identified as Keaton Daucher, 41, yelling inside the home. Wood said Daucher then came out of the home with a shotgun, prompting the two officers to discharge their weapons, killing him. Police said it was unclear if Daucher, who lived at the home, pointed the shotgun at the officers or if he fired any shots. Police said that law enforcement had previously been at the house before Thursday, however it was unclear how many times. WATCH BELOW: Police hold news conference on officer-involved shooting The agency said that the investigation remains ongoing and has been turned over to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which is standard practice for their agency. Neither of the officers were hurt and both have been placed on paid administrative leave pending the investigation, police said.

entry.title: Mbappé partnership signals On’s growing challenge to Nike
entry.summary: French football star Kylian Mbapp has signed a new sponsorship deal with sportswear brand On, following the end of his roughly 20-year relationship with Nike. The Swiss-based company announced Friday that Mbapp will become a global ambassador for On and work directly with Ons product teams on footwear and apparel. This marks a significant entry for the company into the growing football apparel space that has long been dominated by Adidas and Nike. Mbapp, who at just 27 years old is the World Cups all-time goal scorer, will bring his elite perspective into the development and testing of future football products, including Ons Lightspray technology that makes shoes with the help of robots. RELATED STORY | These Nike shoes have a motor and could change how you run forever The length of the deal wasnt disclosed, but an On spokesperson told CNN that the financial agreement includes both cash and equity components. On was founded in 2010, but grew in recognition when Swiss tennis star Roger Federer became an investor in 2019. The brand, initially known for its running and marathon shoes, then expanded into training and tennis shoes. The company represents Ben Shelton, who was a finalist at this years US Open. Signing Mbapp, who currently plays forward for Real Madrid, signals that On is looking to further encroach into its larger competitors territory. RELATED STORY | Caitlin Clark lands $28M endorsement deal with Nike During the recent World Cup, Adidas outfitted Spain and Argentina, both finalists, as well as manufactured the tournaments balls. The German company recently reported record revenue, driven by sales of football jerseys during the month-long tournament. Nike, however, has been less than fortunate: Its shares are hovering around a 12-year low as it deals with a series of problems that CEO Elliott Hill hasnt been able to fix, including customers shopping at trendier brands like On. On is planning to shake up the football category, writing in a press release that its bringing a new energy to the culture that surrounds it. To do that, On also signed Thierry Henry, another French legend, as its new director of Football. It also expanded its relationship with Sydney Schertenleib, a Swiss soccer player that plays for FC Barcelonas womens team.

entry.title: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions - WPBF
entry.summary: Fort Pierce man arrested after raid of illicit drugs worth millions    WPBF
entry.article_text: A Fort Pierce man was arrested after a raid Friday by the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office and U.S. Marshals Service found a massive amount of illicit drugs, including fentanyl and cocaine, worth several million dollars. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office Special Investigations Division, with assistance from the SWAT Team and the U.S. Marshals Service, executed a narcotics-related search warrant at a residence in the 3100 block of S. 24th Street in Fort Pierce. The subject of the investigation, Tony Saunders, 48, was taken into custody. Saunders, a three-time convicted felon who is on federal probation, also had two active warrants related to the sale and delivery of controlled substances. Afterward, Saunders faced additional charges of trafficking in fentanyl, trafficking in cocaine, trafficking in MDPV, manufacturing cocaine, tampering with evidence and possession of marijuana with intent to sell. https://www.facebook.com/stluciesheriff/posts/pfbid0j4igLYhtX4QpfPCZhHkYeREcfiqd9eehsAoAcjVwDWTipnXHZNWyrJLe6gbwukcvl The search resulted in the seizure of approximately 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl, 303 grams of cocaine, 97 grams of marijuana laced with MDPV, and 60 oxycodone pills totaling approximately 6.2 grams, the sheriff's office said. The street value of 4.5 kilograms of fentanyl can range from $150,000 to nearly $1.8 million, depending heavily on its purity, geographic location, and whether it is sold as wholesale powder or broken down into counterfeit pills, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection. The estimated street value of 303 grams of cocaine in the U.S. ranges between roughly $18,180 and $60,600. Detectives also seized assorted ammunition, drug paraphernalia and materials consistent with the preparation and distribution of narcotics. A single kilogram of fentanyl has the potential to kill 500,000 people, making 4.5 kilograms a lethal volume capable of millions of fatal doses, according to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration. “4.5 kilos of fentanyl are 4.5 kilos that will not reach our streets," Sheriff Richard Del Tro said. "Fentanyl is a deadly poison, and those who traffic in it are putting lives at risk for profit. I commend our detectives, SWAT Team, and the U.S. Marshals Service for their commitment to this mission. We will continue to pursue those who traffic dangerous narcotics and do everything within our authority to make St. Lucie County the safest county in Florida.” Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: 'Just heard like two big pop pops': Two men arrested after road rage shooting in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: 'Just heard like two big pop pops': Two men arrested after road rage shooting in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two men were arrested after a road rage incident escalated into a shooting near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. Neighbors reported hearing gunfire at approximately 6:30 p.m. "OK, last night we were trying to put the kids down, and we just heard like two big pop pops," resident Ripley Crawford said. "All we saw was the cars were kind of already pulled to the side, and you could see there was like a crash of sorts." The Port St. Lucie Police Department determined the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between two drivers following a lane change and merging near Southwest Crosstown Parkway. One driver believed he was being followed after the vehicles crossed paths, but investigators found no intentional following. One of the drivers, 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, was traveling with his girlfriend to her home after visiting a local restaurant. The other driver, 41-year-old Dean Plotts, happened to be traveling in the same direction and onto the same streets. As the vehicles continued, the situation escalated into a physical confrontation near SW Brevity Terrace. During the altercation, Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office deputy traveling on SW California Boulevard observed the incident and detained Kukielka. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Later that night, traffic was rerouted as investigators gathered evidence at the scene. "The traffic was just nonstop because they closed California. My neighbor got a call from her daughter in Tennessee that said there was a shooting down here," resident Ernie Lampreda said. Plotts sustained gunshot wounds to his left wrist and legs and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also transported for medical evaluation. Detectives responded to the scene and collected evidence, including shell casings, surveillance video, and dash cam footage that captured portions of the incident. Based on the evidence, witness information, and statements obtained during the investigation, detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Kukielka with attempted homicide – murder, dangerous depraved without premeditation, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 782.04(2). Detectives also determined there was probable cause to charge Plotts with burglary with assault or battery, a felony under Florida Statute 810.02(2)(a). Both men were taken into custody, and the investigation remains ongoing. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Lucie fulfillment center is closing Thursday for a major renovation, leaving hundreds of workers out of a job while others have transferred to different facilities. When Amazon filed its layoff notice in July, 494 employees were listed as affected. Since then, more than 200 workers have transferred to other Amazon locations, according to information provided to CBS12 News. Around 300 employees are expected to take severance as the Port St. Lucie facility shuts down. Local workforce organizations, including CareerSource Research Coast and the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County, have spent recent months holding job fairs and helping affected workers connect with other employers. Lucie County Commissioner Cathy Townsend said the closure highlights the importance of attracting a wider range of businesses to the county. I think we need to be more strategic on the companies we want coming here, Townsend said. My focus would be more on small businesses. See also: CBS12 I-Team: Amendment 3 backers say tax relief could help Florida homeowners stay put The closure is expected to last until at least 2028. Amazon plans to invest about $200 million to renovate and expand the facility. Lucie EDC said the work will include advanced robotics and artificial intelligence capabilities, along with an additional 870,000 square feet. Amazon plans to reopen the facility in the second half of 2028 and hire more than 1,000 employees. Workers who were employed at the facility before the closure will be eligible for rehire when it reopens, according to the EDC. Amazon has said the closure is not expected to impact customers because operations will be handled by other facilities during the renovation.

entry.title: Vero Beach Regional Airport adding 500-space parking lot, but free parking is going away - WFLX
entry.summary: Vero Beach Regional Airport adding 500-space parking lot, but free parking is going away    WFLX
entry.article_text: Vero Beach Regional Airport is adding a new long-term parking lot — but with the newest upgrade, free parking is going away. Vero Beach City Council approved the construction of a new long-term parking lot that will expand capacity from 80 spaces to over 500. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the expansion is driven by new flights coming to the airport. “We have to meet the parking demand,” Dambeck said. Dambeck said the current parking situation is not keeping up. “It looks a little disorganized, especially in the grass parking area. So that’s one thing this parking will really solve,” Dambeck said. When asked why the airport is introducing paid parking, Dambeck said the airport operates without taxpayer dollars and must use the funds to cover the costs of any upgrades to the airport. We first told you about some of the upgrades , including new covered walkways and baggage claim, and a new patio. “The airport is responsible for maintaining its self-sustainability, meaning we don’t take any taxpayer dollars,” said Dambeck. “We have to make sure that our charges will help to to maintain the operations that happen at the airport.” The lot will be built and paid for by Envision Parking Partners. The airport will be responsible for maintaining it. John Mostoller with Envision said travelers will be able to pay through a prepaid option using license plate readers or at the lot gate. “There’s a lot of opportunities to make the experience seamless,” Mostoller said. The new lot will also add cameras and lighting for security. Mostoller said convenience will remain a priority. “No parking spot will be more than two to four minutes from the terminal,” Mostoller said. Some travelers said they will miss the free parking. I mean, that’s — it’s a nice plus to be able to park, especially if it was already free,” traveler Reana Tejada said. Sydney Banak, who was able to park for free during her visit, said she understands the reasoning behind the change. “Free parking is nice,” Sydney said. “But maybe they need to expand the airport or provide more services, so I do understand where they’re coming from with that.” Construction is expected to begin in March and be completed by next summer. entry.title: Port St. Lucie woman accused of elder exploitation, including draining $100K from accounts - WPBF
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie woman accused of elder exploitation, including draining $100K from accounts    WPBF
entry.article_text: A 60-year-old woman was arrested after an investigation by the Port St. Lucie Police Department in alleged exploitation and neglect of an elderly and medically vulnerable man. Barbara Baumgarten is accused of draining around $100,000 from the 85-year-old man's bank accounts and listed herself as a co-borrower on a $616,550 mortgage. She is facing felony charges of grand theft from a person 65 years of age or older, exploitation of an elderly person or disabled adult and neglect of an elderly person or disabled adult. Baumgarten was arrested with help from the U.S. On Thursday, she was booked at the St. Lucie County Jail and remains there on $310,000 bond. Her first appearance was Friday. This investigation began on March 18, when an elderly man was found injured on the floor of his Port St. Lucie home by Baumgarten, his caregiver. The victim initially reported that four men had entered his home and assaulted him. Surveillance footage showed no one entering or leaving the property, and no signs of forced entry or theft. He provided inconsistent accounts of what occurred. Detectives determined the victim was experiencing significant cognitive issues. But detectives continued looking into the victim’s overall well-being and circumstances. The investigation shifted toward concerns of elder exploitation and neglect, and grew into the months-long investigation documented in a 45-page investigative report. As the victim’s physical and cognitive health declined, he became increasingly dependent on Baumgarten, investigators found. They determined that Baumgarten had assumed significant control over the victim’s finances and legal affairs, including power of attorney and healthcare surrogate. Detectives also learned the victim had been isolated from family and friends, and that changes had been made to his estate documents that benefited Baumgarten. Records reviewed by detectives showed there was a decline in his financial accounts from $105,971 in March 2023 to approximately $4,897 by April 2026 . Investigators also uncovered a $616,550 mortgage on Baumgarten’s residence in which the victim was listed as a co-borrower. That is despite the property being solely in Baumgarten’s name and evidence that the victim was reportedly unaware his signature appeared on the mortgage. Detectives worked with healthcare providers, caregivers, family members, financial institutions and other agencies to establish the full extent of the circumstances surrounding the victim’s care and finances. The Florida Department of Children and Families ultimately substantiated allegations of exploitation and determined that the victim lacked the capacity to independently make his own decisions. The victim was removed from Baumgarten’s care, placed under a temporary guardianship, and reunited with his family. "This case serves as a reminder of the importance of looking beyond the initial circumstances when something does not appear right," the police agency said in a news release. "Through an extensive investigation, detectives were able to uncover concerns involving the care, finances, and well-being of a vulnerable member of our community and ultimately help ensure his safety. entry.title: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation - WPTV
entry.summary: Indian River County sheriff announces 50+ arrests in multi-agency human trafficking operation    WPTV
entry.article_text: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office announced more than 50 arrests following a multi-agency, multi-day operation targeting human trafficking and illegal sexual activity in the county.WATCH BELOW: Indian River County Sheriff's Office reveals results of multi-agency operationOperation Late Checkout ran from Sept. 13 in Indian River County. The operation netted over 60 contacts, more than 50 arrests, and three ICE detainers, Sheriff Eric Flowers said during a press conference on Thursday.Flowers announced the results alongside a representative from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement."Agencies involved in the operation included the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Florida Department of Law Enforcement, St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Seminole County Sheriff's Office, Altamonte Springs Police Department, Vero Beach Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, Florida Office of Statewide Prosecutor and the U.S. Attorney's Office," Flowers said.The operation's targeted goal was stopping human trafficking in the Indian River County area, the sheriff's office said.During the operation, several victims were identified, and investigators said ongoing investigations are underway. Flowers said there are no specific arrests on human trafficking charges at this time.One case involved a man who traveled to Indian River County to meet a minor. Flowers said the arrest was the result of the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force working across agencies to apprehend individuals attempting to lure children online."Our team did a great job of getting him off the street," Flowers said.Undercover teams were deployed in a variety of capacities during the operation, the sheriff's office said. Victims' advocates trained to work with trafficking victims were also on hand to speak with women involved in prostitution to determine whether they were being trafficked."We have many ongoing investigations as a result of this," Flowers said.Flowers called the operation unprecedented for Indian River County."We've never had an investigation like this, to my knowledge, in Indian River County with this many agencies involved, with this many arrests in one shot," he said.FDLE Assistant Special Agent in Charge Alfonso Williams said Operation Late Checkout was initiated by FDLE in coordination with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is the first operation of this magnitude conducted in the county."This operation shows that within our communities there are dangerous individuals committing heinous crimes who think they can get away with it," Williams said.Williams said the operation focused on identifying human trafficking victims, reducing the demand for prostitution, and apprehending individuals seeking sexual contact with minors."Our work is far from done," Williams said. "This operation requires a lot of resources and time. We cannot do this work alone, and our success depends on the great partnership and collaboration that you see today."FDLE said it houses the Florida Trafficking Hotline. Anyone who suspects someone is a victim of trafficking can contact the hotline at 1-855-352-7233.READ OPERATION LATE CHECKOUT BELOW:

entry.title: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - WPEC
entry.summary: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    WPEC
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis signed his 18th death warrant of the year Friday. William Reaves , convicted of the 1986 killing of an Indian River County Sheriff's deputy, is set to be executed by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Stark on Oct. According to court records, Reaves shot Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on September 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn’t have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, called the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After the deputy attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away from Raczkowski. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away, at which time Reaves fired four times into Raczkowski’s back. He would die a short time later. Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy as he was high on cocaine and panicked. Reaves was arrested three days later at a bus stop and charged with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. He entered a not guilty plea but was found guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987, with the jury giving a unanimous recommendation for the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor on the case who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury again found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, with the jury voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence. Florida leads the nation in executions, carrying out 15 of them this year after 19 were performed last year, the most in a single year by the state since the U.S. Supreme Court ended a four-year nationwide moratorium on capital punishment in 1976. Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a Polk County woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer in her home. Last Friday, DeSantis signed a warrant for William Lee Thompson, 74, to be executed Oct. 13 for the murder, kidnapping, and sexual battery of Sally Ivester more than 50 years ago in North Miami Beach. Counsel for Reaves quickly filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions for a stay they have also filed regarding Thompson are resolved. See also: Driver hits 120 mph on I-95 before crashing into tree, fence while fleeing FHP Both clients are due the best representation counsel can provide, particularly when both clients are facing a scheduled execution date, stated the motion from Reaves’ counsel Brittney Lacy. The state has conducted 43 executions under DeSantis, or 31 percent of the 140 carried out since 1976. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing for DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves as he is one that, in my opinion, should be a priority case. "It's very frustrating as the Sheriff, Flowers told WPEC last July. We want people to know that we're holding people accountable. And in this case, yes, he's jailed, yes, he's sitting there, but ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences. He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day.

entry.summary: Port St. Lucie hospital MRI technician accused of sexually assaulting sedated patient    WPEC
entry.article_text: A 42-year-old travel MRI technician was arrested after Port St. Lucie police said a patient reported she was sexually assaulted while undergoing an MRI at HCA Florida St. Gabriel Cruz was arrested in Brevard County on the evening of Sept. 16 on a charge of sexual battery involving a physically helpless or incapacitated victim, a first-degree felony, police said. Wasana Chesler is a former patient of St. Lucie Hospital and couldn't believe the news. That's very horrible," Chesler said. "That's very sad." The investigation began Sept. 14 after hospital staff reported that a 64-year-old female patient said she had been sexually assaulted during an MRI the day before at the hospital, 1800 SE Tiffany Ave. Police said the woman had been admitted for medical treatment and was given medication before the MRI that left her significantly drowsy. Detectives identified Cruz as the technician assigned to the procedure. With the hospital’s assistance, investigators obtained video that police said showed Cruz leaving the MRI room after the patient and disposing of materials. See also: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs Those materials were recovered and tested, returning presumptive positive results for male semen, according to police. Cruz had worked at the hospital as a travel MRI technician since Aug. 24 and was hired through a third-party agency, police said. Monica Defoster said she's been to St. Lucie Hospital many times including on Thursday while visiting her husband. She calls the allegations disturbing. They should have more than one person in the MRI room," Defoster said. "You go to the hospital and don't expect something like that." The investigation remains active. Lucie Hospital has cooperated with investigators, police said. Lucie Hospital provided CBS12 News with the following statement: We do not tolerate behavior that jeopardizes the safety or security of our patients. When this serious allegation was reported to us, we contacted law enforcement and ended the individual’s assignment. We have assisted law enforcement throughout its investigation and remain focused on supporting our patient. A hospital spokesman told CBS12 no other complaints have been reported since Cruz stared working there late last month. Cruz's employer could not be reached for comment. He remains behind bars in Brevard County.

entry.summary: Florida Panthers fans got the chance to watch Day 3 of training camp on Saturday as part of this year's Fan Fest at the Iceplex in Fort Lauderdale. Season ticket holders, die-hard fans, and long-time loyalists watched the Panthers practice ahead of their first pre-season game. With the new season on the horizon, fans shared what they are most looking forward to and the excitement was hard to miss. For many, captain Aleksander Barkov's return from injury topped the list. 'How Barkov plays after his comeback from his injuries,' one fan said. WATCH: 'I want the cup,' Florida Panthers fans fired up at Training Camp Fan Fest Florida Panthers fans fired up at Training Camp Fan Fest The Tkachuk brothers were also a major talking point. 'I am so excited for the Tkachuk brothers, obviously. I mean, who's not?' a fan said. Others had their sights set on the ultimate prize. 'I'm excited to see the Stanley Cup finals again, you know, trying to get our third cup. That would be great,' a fan said. When asked about their favorite players, fans were quick to answer. 'Honestly, our captain Barkov,' one fan said. 'Right now I think it's Barkov,' another said. 'Matthew Kachuk,' one fan said. 'I like the Sam's, so I'm gonna say Sam Bennett and Sam Reinhardt just because my daughter's name is Sam. So we go with that,' another fan said. 'I want the cup so I'm saying we're going all the way. There's no percent 100% we're going,' another fan said. entry.summary: Amazon closes Port St. Lucie warehouse for major renovation, hundreds impacted by layoffs    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie fulfillment center is closing Thursday for a major renovation, leaving hundreds of workers out of a job while others have transferred to different facilities. When Amazon filed its layoff notice in July, 494 employees were listed as affected. Since then, more than 200 workers have transferred to other Amazon locations, according to information provided to CBS12 News. Around 300 employees are expected to take severance as the Port St. Lucie facility shuts down. Local workforce organizations, including CareerSource Research Coast and the Economic Development Council of St. Lucie County, have spent recent months holding job fairs and helping affected workers connect with other employers. Lucie County Commissioner Cathy Townsend said the closure highlights the importance of attracting a wider range of businesses to the county. I think we need to be more strategic on the companies we want coming here, Townsend said. My focus would be more on small businesses. See also: CBS12 I-Team: Amendment 3 backers say tax relief could help Florida homeowners stay put The closure is expected to last until at least 2028. Amazon plans to invest about $200 million to renovate and expand the facility. Lucie EDC said the work will include advanced robotics and artificial intelligence capabilities, along with an additional 870,000 square feet. Amazon plans to reopen the facility in the second half of 2028 and hire more than 1,000 employees. Workers who were employed at the facility before the closure will be eligible for rehire when it reopens, according to the EDC. Amazon has said the closure is not expected to impact customers because operations will be handled by other facilities during the renovation.

entry.title: Florida governor signs death warrant for William Reaves Jr., convicted of killing Indian River County deputy - WFLX
entry.summary: Florida governor signs death warrant for William Reaves Jr., convicted of killing Indian River County deputy    WFLX
entry.article_text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has signed a death warrant for 77-year-old William Reaves Jr., the man convicted of murdering Indian River County Sheriff’s Deputy Richard Raczkoski in 1986. The execution is scheduled for Tuesday, Oct. Reaves was convicted of murdereing Raczkoski on Sept. 23, 1986, after a confrontation at a convenience store. Deputy Raczkoski had responded to a 911 call at the store when he encountered Reaves. During a conversation between the two, a gun fell from Reaves’s shorts. Deputy Raczkoski placed his knee on the weapon. Reaves then pushed the deputy away, grabbed the gun and pointed it at Deputy Raczkoski’s face. As Deputy Raczkoski attempted to draw his own weapon, Reaves said, “I wouldn’t do that if I were you.” The deputy backed away, turned, and ran. Reaves fired seven rounds, striking Deputy Raczkoski four times. Reaves was tried in the 19th Judicial Circuit in Indian River County. On direct appeal, the Florida Supreme Court reversed the initial conviction and remanded the case for a new trial. On remand, Reaves was again convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death on March 6, 1992, in Vero Beach. The Florida Supreme Court affirmed the conviction and death sentence on April 7, 1994. The United States Supreme Court denied Reaves’s petition for a writ of certiorari on Nov. Reaves pursued numerous postconviction challenges in both state and federal courts over the following decades. District Court for the Southern District of Florida granted Reaves’s federal petition for a writ of habeas corpus. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit overturned that ruling and ordered that the petition be denied. Additional postconviction motions and petitions were subsequently denied, and those denials were affirmed on appeal. Executive clemency was also considered and denied. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier, in his letter recommending the warrant, wrote that “the record is legally sufficient to support the issuance of a death warrant,” and confirmed that “there are no stays of execution issued by any court of competent jurisdiction in this cause.” The execution is scheduled to take place at Florida State Prison in Raiford. If carried out as scheduled, it will come 40 years after the murder of Deputy Raczkoski.

entry.title: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - WPEC
entry.summary: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    WPEC
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis signed his 18th death warrant of the year Friday. William Reaves , convicted of the 1986 killing of an Indian River County Sheriff's deputy, is set to be executed by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Stark on Oct. According to court records, Reaves shot Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on September 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn’t have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, called the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After the deputy attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away from Raczkowski. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away, at which time Reaves fired four times into Raczkowski’s back. He would die a short time later. Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy as he was high on cocaine and panicked. Reaves was arrested three days later at a bus stop and charged with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. He entered a not guilty plea but was found guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987, with the jury giving a unanimous recommendation for the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor on the case who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury again found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, with the jury voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence. Florida leads the nation in executions, carrying out 15 of them this year after 19 were performed last year, the most in a single year by the state since the U.S. Supreme Court ended a four-year nationwide moratorium on capital punishment in 1976. Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a Polk County woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer in her home. Last Friday, DeSantis signed a warrant for William Lee Thompson, 74, to be executed Oct. 13 for the murder, kidnapping, and sexual battery of Sally Ivester more than 50 years ago in North Miami Beach. Counsel for Reaves quickly filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions for a stay they have also filed regarding Thompson are resolved. See also: Driver hits 120 mph on I-95 before crashing into tree, fence while fleeing FHP Both clients are due the best representation counsel can provide, particularly when both clients are facing a scheduled execution date, stated the motion from Reaves’ counsel Brittney Lacy. The state has conducted 43 executions under DeSantis, or 31 percent of the 140 carried out since 1976. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing for DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves as he is one that, in my opinion, should be a priority case. "It's very frustrating as the Sheriff, Flowers told WPEC last July. We want people to know that we're holding people accountable. And in this case, yes, he's jailed, yes, he's sitting there, but ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences. He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day.

entry.article_text: A 60-year-old woman was arrested after an investigation by the Port St. Lucie Police Department in alleged exploitation and neglect of an elderly and medically vulnerable man. Barbara Baumgarten is accused of draining around $100,000 from the 85-year-old man's bank accounts and listed herself as a co-borrower on a $616,550 mortgage. She is facing felony charges of grand theft from a person 65 years of age or older, exploitation of an elderly person or disabled adult and neglect of an elderly person or disabled adult. Baumgarten was arrested with help from the U.S. On Thursday, she was booked at the St. Lucie County Jail and remains there on $310,000 bond. Her first appearance was Friday. This investigation began on March 18, when an elderly man was found injured on the floor of his Port St. Lucie home by Baumgarten, his caregiver. The victim initially reported that four men had entered his home and assaulted him. Surveillance footage showed no one entering or leaving the property, and no signs of forced entry or theft. He provided inconsistent accounts of what occurred. Detectives determined the victim was experiencing significant cognitive issues. But detectives continued looking into the victim’s overall well-being and circumstances. The investigation shifted toward concerns of elder exploitation and neglect, and grew into the months-long investigation documented in a 45-page investigative report. As the victim’s physical and cognitive health declined, he became increasingly dependent on Baumgarten, investigators found. They determined that Baumgarten had assumed significant control over the victim’s finances and legal affairs, including power of attorney and healthcare surrogate. Detectives also learned the victim had been isolated from family and friends, and that changes had been made to his estate documents that benefited Baumgarten. Records reviewed by detectives showed there was a decline in his financial accounts from $105,971 in March 2023 to approximately $4,897 by April 2026 . Investigators also uncovered a $616,550 mortgage on Baumgarten’s residence in which the victim was listed as a co-borrower. That is despite the property being solely in Baumgarten’s name and evidence that the victim was reportedly unaware his signature appeared on the mortgage. Detectives worked with healthcare providers, caregivers, family members, financial institutions and other agencies to establish the full extent of the circumstances surrounding the victim’s care and finances. The Florida Department of Children and Families ultimately substantiated allegations of exploitation and determined that the victim lacked the capacity to independently make his own decisions. The victim was removed from Baumgarten’s care, placed under a temporary guardianship, and reunited with his family. "This case serves as a reminder of the importance of looking beyond the initial circumstances when something does not appear right," the police agency said in a news release. "Through an extensive investigation, detectives were able to uncover concerns involving the care, finances, and well-being of a vulnerable member of our community and ultimately help ensure his safety. entry.title: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986 - cbs12.com
entry.summary: DeSantis signs death warrant for man who killed Indian River County deputy in 1986    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Ron DeSantis signed his 18th death warrant of the year Friday. William Reaves , convicted of the 1986 killing of an Indian River County Sheriff's deputy, is set to be executed by lethal injection at Florida State Prison in Stark on Oct. According to court records, Reaves shot Deputy Sheriff Richard Raczkowski four times in the back outside a Zippy Mart convenience store near Vero Beach on September 23, 1986. Reaves had called 911 from a pay phone because he didn’t have money for a cab. Raczkowski, who was dispatched to the call, called the 911 dispatcher to order a cab for Reaves and to inquire about outstanding warrants. During this time, Reaves said a gun fell out of his pants. After the deputy attempted to block Reaves from retrieving the gun, a struggle ensued and Reaves wrestled the weapon away from Raczkowski. The deputy asked Reaves not to kill him and turned to run away, at which time Reaves fired four times into Raczkowski’s back. He would die a short time later. Reaves went to the home of a friend, who later told police Reaves confessed to shooting the deputy as he was high on cocaine and panicked. Reaves was arrested three days later at a bus stop and charged with first-degree murder, possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and trafficking in cocaine. He entered a not guilty plea but was found guilty of first-degree murder in September 1987, with the jury giving a unanimous recommendation for the death penalty. The Florida Supreme Court reversed the conviction and sentence in 1991, finding the trial court erred by allowing a prosecutor on the case who had previously defended Reaves in a criminal matter. A second jury again found Reaves guilty of first-degree murder in February 1992, with the jury voting 10-2 to recommend a death sentence. Florida leads the nation in executions, carrying out 15 of them this year after 19 were performed last year, the most in a single year by the state since the U.S. Supreme Court ended a four-year nationwide moratorium on capital punishment in 1976. Curtis Wilkie Beasley, 77, is scheduled for execution on Sept. 29 for the 1995 murder of a Polk County woman who was bludgeoned with a hammer in her home. Last Friday, DeSantis signed a warrant for William Lee Thompson, 74, to be executed Oct. 13 for the murder, kidnapping, and sexual battery of Sally Ivester more than 50 years ago in North Miami Beach. Counsel for Reaves quickly filed a motion Friday for a stay until pending motions for a stay they have also filed regarding Thompson are resolved. See also: Driver hits 120 mph on I-95 before crashing into tree, fence while fleeing FHP Both clients are due the best representation counsel can provide, particularly when both clients are facing a scheduled execution date, stated the motion from Reaves’ counsel Brittney Lacy. The state has conducted 43 executions under DeSantis, or 31 percent of the 140 carried out since 1976. Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers has been pushing for DeSantis to sign the warrant for Reaves as he is one that, in my opinion, should be a priority case. "It's very frustrating as the Sheriff, Flowers told WPEC last July. We want people to know that we're holding people accountable. And in this case, yes, he's jailed, yes, he's sitting there, but ultimately it was decided a long time ago that he would face the death penalty, and it's time for him to actually face the consequences. He's exhausted all of his appeals. Many other cases just like his have resulted in execution, and for some reason, he continues to cost us taxpayer dollars every single day.

entry.title: 'I want the cup,' Florida Panthers fans fired up at Training Camp Fan Fest
entry.summary: Florida Panthers fans got the chance to watch Day 3 of training camp on Saturday as part of this year's Fan Fest at the Iceplex in Fort Lauderdale. Season ticket holders, die hard fans and long time loyalist watched the Panthers practice ahead of thier first pre-seaon game. With the new season on the horizon, fans shared what they are most looking forward to and the excitement was hard to miss. For many, captain Aleksander Barkov's return from injury topped the list. 'How Barkov plays after his comeback from his injuries,' one fan said. The Tkachuk brothers were also a major talking point. 'I am so excited for the Tkachuk brothers, obviously. I mean, who's not?' a fan said. Others had their sights set on the ultimate prize. 'I'm excited to see the Stanley Cup finals again, you know, trying to get our third cup. That would be great,' a fan said. When asked about their favorite players, fans were quick to answer. 'Honestly, our captain Barkov,' one fan said. 'Right now I think it's Barkov,' another said. 'Matthew Tkachuk,' one fan said. 'I like the Sam's, so I'm gonna say Sam Bennett and Sam Reinhart just because my daughter's name is Sam. So we go with that,' another fan said. Panthers fans also had plenty to say about their own reputation in the NHL. 'We're a hardcore diehards. We love our Cats,' one fan said. 'We're the best fans in the NHL,' another said. 'People complain about our fans being bandwagon. I say whatever with that,' a fan said. As for the Panthers' playoff and championship odds, fans were not short on confidence. 'All the way 99,' one fan said. 'I think they have the shot to make it to the playoffs easy. For the finals, I think we can do it. We just need to get some puck luck and stay healthy,' another said. 'With our roster right now. I believe that we have 100% chance to make the playoffs and I believe that we will win another Stanley Cup,' a fan said. 'I want the cup so I'm saying we're going all the way. There's no percent 100% we're going,' another fan said. The Panthers play their first preseason home game on Sunday against the defending champions, the Carolina Hurricanes.

entry.title: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee - cbs12.com
entry.summary: Martin County health officials warn of harmful algae near Lake Okeechobee    cbs12.com
entry.article_text: Health officials have issued a blue-green algae health alert for an area of Lake Okeechobee after water samples detected harmful toxins. The Florida Department of Health in Martin County said the alert covers the Lake Okeechobee NES135 area and was issued in response to samples collected Sept. The area is located on the north shore of the lake at J&S Fish Camp in Martin County. Residents and visitors should use caution in and around the lake, officials said. People should not drink, swim, wade, use personal watercraft or otherwise come into contact with water where a visible algae bloom is present. Health officials also advised people to keep pets and livestock away from affected water. Anyone who comes into contact with algae, discolored water or water with an unpleasant odor should wash their skin and clothing with soap and water, according to the department. Officials said contaminated water should not be used for cooking or washing dishes because boiling does not remove algae toxins. Blue-green algae are bacteria commonly found in Florida freshwater. Blooms can discolor water and create floating mats, scum, foam or paint-like material on the surface, sometimes with an unpleasant odor. The blooms can produce toxins that may harm people, pets and aquatic life. Children, older adults and people with weakened immune systems may be at risk even at low toxin concentrations and should avoid exposure, health officials said. RELATED: 'Influence campaign': Okeechobee County leaders want to change Lake O's narrative Officials said it is safe to eat fillets from healthy freshwater fish caught in lakes experiencing blooms if the fillets are rinsed with tap or bottled water, the guts are discarded and the fish is thoroughly cooked. People should not eat shellfish from waters with algae blooms. The Florida Department of Environmental Protection monitors reported blooms and collects samples for analysis. The public can report an algae bloom online at ReportAlgalBloom.com or call 1-855-305-3903 . Anyone who develops symptoms after exposure to a harmful algae bloom can call the Florida Poison Information Center at 800-222-1222 . Pet owners who believe an animal became ill after exposure should contact a veterinarian. For health questions about blue-green algae, call DOH-Martin at 772-221-4090 .

entry.title: 'Just heard like two big pop pops': Two men arrested after road rage shooting in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: 'Just heard like two big pop pops': Two men arrested after road rage shooting in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: Two men were arrested after a road rage incident escalated into a shooting near Southwest California Boulevard and Southwest Brevity Terrace. Neighbors reported hearing gunfire at approximately 6:30 p.m. "OK, last night we were trying to put the kids down, and we just heard like two big pop pops," resident Ripley Crawford said. "All we saw was the cars were kind of already pulled to the side, and you could see there was like a crash of sorts." The Port St. Lucie Police Department determined the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between two drivers following a lane change and merging near Southwest Crosstown Parkway. One driver believed he was being followed after the vehicles crossed paths, but investigators found no intentional following. One of the drivers, 57-year-old Tylon Kukielka, was traveling with his girlfriend to her home after visiting a local restaurant. The other driver, 41-year-old Dean Plotts, happened to be traveling in the same direction and onto the same streets. As the vehicles continued, the situation escalated into a physical confrontation near SW Brevity Terrace. During the altercation, Kukielka fired a handgun, striking Plotts twice. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office deputy traveling on SW California Boulevard observed the incident and detained Kukielka. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Later that night, traffic was rerouted as investigators gathered evidence at the scene. "The traffic was just nonstop because they closed California. My neighbor got a call from her daughter in Tennessee that said there was a shooting down here," resident Ernie Lampreda said. Plotts sustained gunshot wounds to his left wrist and legs and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital for treatment. Kukielka was also transported for medical evaluation. Detectives responded to the scene and collected evidence, including shell casings, surveillance video, and dash cam footage that captured portions of the incident. Based on the evidence, witness information, and statements obtained during the investigation, detectives determined there was probable cause to charge Kukielka with attempted homicide – murder, dangerous depraved without premeditation, a first-degree felony under Florida Statute 782.04(2). Detectives also determined there was probable cause to charge Plotts with burglary with assault or battery, a felony under Florida Statute 810.02(2)(a). Both men were taken into custody, and the investigation remains ongoing. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25

entry.title: West Palm Beach woman charged with animal cruelty after 11 dogs found in filthy cages at her home
entry.summary: A West Palm Beach woman is facing multiple animal cruelty charges after investigators said 11 dogs were found living in cages containing accumulated urine and feces inside her home. Deputies reported smelling a strong odor of urine and feces and hearing numerous dogs barking inside. Palm Beach County Animal Care and Control was called to the home. Investigators said Torres identified 13 dogs as hers, 11 of which she ultimately surrendered to animal control. According to investigators, several dogs were being kept in wire cages containing accumulated feces, urine-soaked clothing and other debris. entry.title: Tropical Storm Fay forms in Atlantic, expected to strengthen Sunday
entry.summary: Tropical Storm Fay formed in the Atlantic Ocean Sunday morning as the system strengthened hundreds of miles southwest of the Azores. As of the 5 a.m. EDT advisory, Fay had maximum sustained winds of 45 mph and was located about 450 miles southwest of the Azores. The storm was moving north-northeast at 5 mph. Fay is a compact storm, with tropical-storm-force winds extending up to about 45 miles from its center. Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center expect Fay to strengthen further Sunday, with maximum sustained winds forecast to reach 60 mph later in the day. The storm is expected to continue moving generally north-northeast for about another day before turning toward the southwest Monday as a ridge builds to its north. Fay's opportunity to strengthen is expected to be short-lived. Increasing wind shear and dry air are forecast to cause the storm to weaken beginning Monday. The National Hurricane Center forecasts Fay to become a post-tropical remnant low by Tuesday and dissipate by the end of the week. There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect, and the storm currently poses no hazards to land. entry.title: Porto Sol residents in Royal Palm Beach demand relief as neighborhood streets flood knee-deep
entry.summary: Residents in the Porto Sol community in Royal Palm Beach are demanding answers after soaking rains left neighborhood streets flooded knee-deep in some areas. Joseph Pankowski, a resident, described the conditions outside his home. WATCH WPTV'S COVERAGE BELOW: Porto Sol residents in Royal Palm Beach demand relief as neighborhood streets flood knee-deep 'This is like a lake, a river here,' Pankowski said. Fellow resident Leighton Forbes said the flooding has made daily life challenging and described it as the worst he has ever seen in the neighborhood. 'It's gotten so bad, it's difficult to do anything here,' Forbes said. 'We didn't think it was going to be this bad. The water when I got homeI could see debris up to here so it went under my garage,' Forbes said. Resident Jeff Duggins described the scene on neighborhood streets. 'There's actually cars parking outside of their house and they're rolling their pants up and taking off their shoes and trying to walk home,' Duggins said. Pankowski said neighbors are frustrated with the lack of response and questioned where HOA fees are going. 'What about getting pump trucks. We pay HOA money, why aren't we having our money to take care of this,' Pankowski said. Pankowski also pointed to passing vehicles making conditions worse. 'You see like this guy here. They just come flying through and then they just push everything up,' Pankowski said. With more rain potentially on the way, Forbes said the uncertainty is weighing on the community. 'If we get any more rain, what's going to happen,' Forbes said. WPTV reached out to the HOA management for Porto Sol to find out how they plan to address the problem. They received our message, but we are still waiting to hear back. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI.
